name: Habitat Enhancement and Restoration Program (HERP)
summary: California state grants for habitat restoration projects such as coast, wetland and grassland restoration, wildlife corridors and fish passage, applied for through the WCB Project Portal.

steps: Technical review and scoring of the full application
Funding decision at a public WCB Board meeting

eligibility.rule: Project receives a CDFW recommendation and provides long-term maintenance after completion
Project provides biodiversity, climate action, or public access benefits
Implementation applications include intermediate or advanced design plans
No individual involved in planning the call or negotiating the grant for the public receives or benefits from funds
Standard funding: 501(c)(3) nonprofit, local/state/federal agency, or California Native American tribe

documents: Full list of assessor’s parcel numbers for projects with more than five parcels

geography.quote: HERP projects are distributed throughout California and all habitat types.

access.quote: WCB is now accepting pre-applications through the new WCB Project Portal.

co_finance_required.quote: Cost share is not required but may be beneficial, in particular to complete a larger project.

effort.quote: Applicants will first submit a Pre-application.
If selected, WCB will invite you to submit a Full Application via email.
All eligible and complete Full Applications will be evaluated and scored by technical
in preparation for presentation at a public WCB Board meeting. WCB’s voting members have sole and absolute discretion to approve a project for funding.

eligibility.quote: HERP projects must receive a recommendation from the California Department of Fish and Wildlife and provide for long-term maintenance following project completion.

All projects shall provide one or more of the following benefits, as identified in WCB's Strategic Plan:  Protected or restored biodiversity;  Climate change action; and/or  Expanded public access to nature.
Implementation applications must include intermediate or advanced design plans (e.g., design plans at ~65% level of development or higher).

Any individual who has participated in planning or setting priorities for a specific solicitation or who will participate in any part of the grant development and negotiation process on behalf of the public is ineligible to receive funds or personally benefit from funds awarded through these guidelines.

Unless otherwise limited by applicable funding sources or individual program guidelines, WCB has the authority under FGC section 1350(c) to award grants to 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations, local governmental agencies, federal agencies, state agencies, and California Native American tribes.

after_award.quote: All grantees doing restoration, development, scientific studies, and planning will be required to provide a final report.
